newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to negotiate with BNFL on nuclear deal.
newsitem.headline: Canada to negotiate with BNFL on nuclear deal.

text.p: The Canadian government said on Monday it would negotiate with a consortium led by a unit of British Nuclear Fuels Plc (BNFL) on the privatization of one of its flagship nuclear research laboratories.

The Canadian Nuclear Projects Ltd (CNP) proposal to operate the Whiteshell laboratories in Manitoba was chosen over one made by a consortium led by Toronto's Golder Group, a government spokesman said.

CNP is 55 percent owned by BNFL's U.S. subsidiary, British Nuclear Fuels Inc., in partnership with three Canadian firms -- Wardrop Engineering (20 percent), Acres International (20 percent) and SENES Consultants (5 percent).
BNFL Plc, is a British government-owned company active in decommissioning nuclear sites.

The Irish government complained in February about systems failures and incidents at British Nuclear facilities, but Natural Resources Minister Anne McLellan said she was not concerned there would be problems in Canada.
"It is important to point out that the company involved in this consortium is of course the US subsidiary," she told Reuters.
"We certainly have looked at the way they have conducted themselves in the United States and at this point we have no concerns in that regard."

The government agency Atomic Energy of Canada Ltd (AECL), which owns Whiteshell, was hit by a 40 percent cut to its research and development funding, forcing it to concentrate on its CANDU nuclear reactor program.
Whiteshell conducts research into nuclear reactor safety and nuclear waste management.
